objective: At the owner's request ('pursue ii', UNIFORM-SPHERES-20261107-001's recommendation (ii), rated Payoff 1/3 - Incremental, Concreteness 3/3 - Ready): decide whether any uniform knot law other than the Fano plane contradicts itself. With uniform signs the count never forces a uniform law's lines (UNIFORM-SPHERES-20261107-001A), so any such contradiction is of the Fano kind (a non-2-colourable cubic triple system). Prove that a law whose symmetries are transitive on points and on lines has a brace for its incidence graph, so that McCuaig's theorem leaves only the Fano plane, and check it on a census of Cayley laws. Serves question 9 (what a uniform law can and cannot do).
status: Complete 2026-11-07: a simple cubic triple system transitive on points and lines has a brace for its incidence graph, so by Seymour's dictionary and McCuaig's theorem the Fano plane is its only non-2-colourable case; with non-constant uniform signs satisfied by the all-zero assignment, the Fano plane is the only uniform knot law that contradicts itself (439 Cayley laws agree). Recommendation: Continue to (i), laws that distinguish places by themselves, scoping first (Payoff 3/3 Barrier, Concreteness 1/3 Stated).
stop_rule: Stop when the uniform contradictions are classified by proof, or an obstruction to the proof is found and explained.
title: The Fano plane is the only uniform law that contradicts itself
